items.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And I have it with Jake Hanna, the drummer. ... We love to play together.

ctx.x: Can you tell us other musicians that you’ve had that chemistry with?

Oh let me see. Well there’s a lot of them. I had it with Sweets Edison, he’s here at the festival, you know. And I have it with Jake Hanna, the drummer. And of course I have it with Ray Brown to a great extent. We love to play together. So there could be more but I can’t name them all.
Could you also explain to guitarists how that it takes an impeccable sense of time to play in a trio with no drums.

items.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: His lengthy list of recordings include work with SuperSax, Oscar Peterson, Herb Ellis and Carl Fontana.

ctx.x: Drummer Jake Hanna has been the spark plug behind some of this country’s hottest jazz ensembles. A native of Boston, he was born on April 4, 1931 and received his first drum lessons from Stanley Spector. In the mid 50s, Jake played with a succession of jazz stars including Woody Herman, Marian McPartland and Maynard Ferguson. He has had a steady career on both coasts, moving to Los Angeles in 1970 with the Merv Griffin Show. His lengthy list of recordings include work with SuperSax, Oscar Peterson, Herb Ellis and…
Jake is the subject of a chapter in Marian McPartland’s book All in Good Time. He continues to lead a busy schedule of recording and appearances at jazz clubs and festivals.
